Consent, privacy and data-principal rights

A source-linked technical walkthrough. Trace the flow, explain the boundary, then test the failure path.

After this session, you can:
  • Explain purpose-bound consent
  • Trace access, correction and erasure
  • Reconcile retention and legal hold

Technical flow

Every hand-off is a control boundary: on failure the flow holds, refers or denies — it never skips ahead.

  1. 01Notice + purpose
  2. 02Consent event
  3. 03Permitted processing
  4. 04Rights request
  5. 05Retention / legal-hold decision
  6. 06Fulfilment evidence

1. Consent is a ledger

Notice version, language, purpose, data categories, channel, actor and proof are recorded as a lifecycle. Withdrawal stops future optional processing without erasing required historical evidence.

2. Rights are workflows

Access, correction, nomination and erasure requests authenticate the person, gather scoped data, run SLA clocks and retain fulfilment evidence. They are not ad-hoc database edits.

3. Retention wins explicitly

Regulatory retention, active contracts, disputes and legal holds may delay erasure. The response records the lawful reason and later resumes deletion or redaction when the hold clears.
